The Walking Dead is a story-driven adventure game.
Though it feels more like an interactive story, than an actual game, it still got me from the first minute.
There is not much gameplay in it, you walk here and there and talk to other people and every now and then you need to make choices (for most of them there is a short time limit).
There are a lot likable (and not so likable) characters. Together with the choices you have to make, it is a thrilling and emotional experience.

Highly recommended if you like story-driven games and/or adventures.

Loved every part of this game.
Some people may argue that your choices don't actually matter, and I'd say they are not wrong... But they are not right either. The choices you make in the game may not have an impact on the end itself, but it will have an impact on how the story gets told to you. Will you become a respectable man, or will you be an asshole throughout the entire game? The choice is yours. 

What does matter here is the travel, and not the destination.

The graphics are enjoyable; you really feel like you're part of the original comics universe. The game developpers also had the good idea to create their own story and not simply take the comics story. This is not a simple adaptation of the comics books, this is a parallel story which does not make some fan services; the references to the books are smart and really not invasive.

All in all, this is a simple, yet very enjoyable story-driven point-and-click, merging some humor and a lot of drama in a good and smart enough interactive story.

Turn the lights off, and play it alone or with someone else, and discuss about the choices you should make or should have made.

A must play!

You know what I love about this game?

The zombies barely matter.

Sure, they’re everywhere. Walking corpses. Empty eyes. Hungry mouths. Civilization collapsing around them.

Cute.

But the real monsters?

They still know how to talk.

That’s what The Walking Dead understands perfectly.

Take away electricity. Take away laws. Take away supermarkets, police, comfortable little houses and all those rules people hide behind...

Then watch what happens.

Everybody starts showing you who they really are.

And I love watching that happen.

Then there’s Lee.

A man with a past nobody wants to forgive, suddenly responsible for a little girl who has absolutely no business surviving in this world.

Clementine.

And somehow, against everything happening around them, protecting her becomes more important than the apocalypse itself.

I respect that.

Because this game constantly puts people in your hands and asks you to decide.

Who gets trusted?

Who gets protected?

Who gets another chance?

And sometimes...

Who gets left behind?

Everyone looks at Lee expecting him to make the right decision.

That’s adorable.

There is no right decision.

There’s just the decision you make...

and everyone else learning to live with it.

That’s power.

The choices are what make this game unforgettable. People remember what you say. They remember who you defended. They remember when you hesitated.

And eventually you start remembering too.

That’s the disturbing part.

I started this game thinking I’d be watching people survive a zombie apocalypse.

Instead, I found myself judging them.

Watching them.

Deciding who I trusted.

And occasionally smiling when somebody proved me right.

The story gets darker and more personal until suddenly you realize you actually care about these people.

Especially Clementine.

That annoyed me.

I wasn’t supposed to get attached.

But I did.

And by the end...

Well.

Let’s just say the game managed to make me sit quietly through the credits.

Do you understand how difficult that is?

Ten out of ten.

Brutal. Emotional. Uncomfortably human.

A masterpiece that understands the apocalypse doesn’t turn people into monsters.

It just removes the audience they were behaving for.

This game is called the Walking Dead. But it's not because of the post apocalyptic theme.

It's because you will be dead inside when you finish this game.

If you want an emotional rollercoaster, TTG's TWD is your game.
You're going to take care of a little girl, that'll get close to your heart, I promise.

You're living the full story. In the game, you need to make a choice in almost any dialogue, make a decision, and these can affect the progress of the game.

It's more of an emotional mood than an action. Human relationships are at the forefront, and the way you communicate with those around you influences the story.

The game is generally in the style of point and click. This means that you need to press the right place, especially in action scenes. In this way, you feel like you are really doing that action.

The story ends very impressively.

[h3]The Walking Dead Season 1[/h3]

[b][i]The Walking Dead: Season 1[/i][/b] is a [i]pretty strange game to judge by normal standards[/i]. Mechanically there honestly isnt that much going on. You walk around small locations, talk with people, look for some items, make a bunch of choices and occasionally deal with QTEs. But after finishing it, [i]gameplay is probably the last thing I’d think about[/i].

What actually carries the game is the [b][u]story and the characters[/u][/b]. Despite being a zombie game, [i]zombies rarely feel like the main problem[/i]. Most of the [i]tension comes from the people around u[/i] – everyone is scared,tired,stressed,and usually has their own idea of what the group should do. Because of that, even pretty simple situations can turn into serious conflicts.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=2364271636

[b]Lee[/b] is probably the main [i]reason why the story works as well as it does[/i]. He has his own past/mistakes, so he never feels like an empty character, but you still [i]have enough control over how he behaves to make ur version of him feel kinda personal[/i].

And then there’s Clementine. I already knew she was important before playing, but I didn’t expect her relationship with Lee to [i]feel this natural[/i]. It develops slowly,without constantly trying to remind you how emotional it is. At first Lee is simply trying to protect her, but later you start thinking more about what you say around her, what she sees you doing and what kind of example you’re giving her.

That’s also where the choice system works best.
Obviously, [b]not every decision changes the story[/b] in some huge way. The overall plot is much [i]more fixed than the game first makes it look[/i], and certain events happen regardless of what you choose. But I don’t think that makes the choices pointless. Their main purpose is to change your relationships with people and make you actually think about what you’re doing.

A lot of decisions also [i]don’t have one clearly correct answer[/i]. Sometimes both options are understandable, sometimes both are pretty bad, and sometimes you simply don’t have enough time to think properly. That [b]moral ambiguity[/b] is probably one of the strongest parts of the game.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3776482152

The actual [b]gameplay is much less interesting[/b], but it also never really tries to be the main focus. [i]Exploration – simple, puzzles – basic, and action scenes mostly exist to keep the pacing moving[/i]. The controls and animations can feel old sometimes, but for this kind of game I don’t think that’s a huge issue. It knows that dialogue and characters are the important part and stays focused on that.

[b]Visually[/b], I still really like how it looks. [i]The comic-book style fits the setting perfectly and helps the game age much better than if it had tried to look realistic[/i]. The [i]soundtrack is pretty minimalistic, and the voice acting is consistently good[/i], which matters a lot in a game where such a huge part of the experience is just listening to people talk.

I also liked how the [i]slower moments can be just as important as the big dramatic ones[/i]. Sitting somewhere and talking with the group, checking on Clementine or just walking around a temporary safe place can tell you more about the characters than another zombie attack would.

Of course, [b]it has flaws[/b]. The choice system sometimes creates [b][i]an illusion of freedom[/i][/b] that isn’t really there, some gameplay sections are very basic, and technically the game definitely shows its age. But none of that seriously hurt the experience for me.

https://steamcommunity.com/sharedfiles/filedetails/?id=3538614463

So yeah I can understand why The Walking Dead: Season 1 is still the game people immediately mention when talking about Telltale. It doesn’t have amazing gameplay or some insanely complicated branching story. [i]It’s simply a very well-told character story where your choices make the journey feel personal, even if they don’t completely rewrite where it ends[/i].

And more than anything, [b]Lee and Clementine are what I’ll probably remember from it[/b]. Their relationship never felt forced, and by the end I was much more invested in what happened to them than I expected to be.

The Walking Dead is an episodic interactive story adventure developed and published by Telltale Games based on The Walking Dead comic book series.  The game consist of five separate chapters which we released spread out across 2012. 

The game takes place shortly after the start of a zombie apocalypse in the US state of Georgia. Most of the characters are all unique to the game. You play the role of a university professor, who is also a convicted murderer. You rescue and care for a little called called Clementine.  

Very much unlike other adventure games, there is hardly any puzzle solving to be found in The Walking Dead; it focuses mainly on the story and character development and relationships. The story is heavily effected by dialogue choices and actions taken during quick time events - these choices will often lead to game altering changes such as a character being killed off etc.  All of the choices and events from one episode are carried over onto the next. I have also leaned since completing the game; that Telltale actually tracked the choices made too, and helped them to influence their writing in later episodes in the story. 

You play the game mainly in a third person perspective and the camera changes depending on the scenery and objects around the player. You are constantly in communication with the rest of your group of survivors; you will build friendships, enemies and you will bond with most of the characters in someway. You will be emotionally attached to them, especially the young child, Clementine. While most of the game is also based around the dialogue, there are a number of quick time events throughout the series, normally I am not a huge fan of QTEs, but these are required in the story in order to get their point across and to at least keep you conscious of your surroundings when playing. 

Graphics do not play a huge role in this game; it is by far the least important aspect to be seen. Saying that; the art style is nice and many developers should learn from this that having top of the range graphics isn't always the be all and end all for when creating a game. 

The story is probably the best I have ever seen/heard in a video game; you will be drawn in from the minute you start interacting with different characters, learning about their backstory, building bonds. There are so many twists and turns in the story to keep you guessing too. By the end, if you are like me, you'll be a complete and utter emotional wreck with that the cast have gone through. This is one of the only games that has almost brought me to tears. 

Since the game doesn't resolve around fast paced action other than the QTEs, there isn't any real difficulty; there is no "wrong" choice when it comes to dialogue, you are free to let the story develop however you choose. 

Each of the chapters level design are so well thought out; there are tons of objects to interact with, pick up and use with you in future situations. If it is of any interest; then you will be able to do something with it. The art style really gets across how doomed the civilized world is in the ruined remains of cities and towns. 

I have run through The Walking Dead two times now; my first play through was back when it originally came out during the sporadic release of the episodes, and just recently when I played through them all in a big binge. It is very rare that I want to play through a game again a second time; and The Walking Dead offers exactly the same excitement the second time around; you make different choices allowing the story to change and adapt to them. The whole game takes about fourteen hours to get through all of the chapters; so you are looking at a really good length game/story too. 

The game can be played using a controller too - which is a nice touch given that this is the perfect sort you could play while sitting back on the sofa and soaking up the story.  I also had no other technical problems while playing. 

Most people already have The Walking Dead; and most will probably have already played it given it's age now. But this is a genre defining game that has brought the adventure games right back to the forefront of PC gaming. You need to experience this heart wrenching tale. Even if zombies aren't your thing; you will get emotionally hooked from the get go. Do your self a favor and play this masterpiece.

The story is incredible, full of emotion and tension, and the characters are unforgettable.

This game isn’t about crazy action it’s about interacting with people, making moral choices, and teaching Clementine how to survive in a harsh world.

This game is one of the most emotional and addictive games I've ever played. The plot of the game is about surviving in a world filled with zombies and the difficult choices the main character, Lee Everett, has to make. Lee is a former history teacher who gets into an accident at the beginning of the game and meets a little girl named Clementine. He decides to protect her and take care of her as his daughter. Together, they join a group of other survivors and try to find a safe place.

The game consists of five episodes, each offering unique situations and characters. The game relies heavily on the player's decisions, which affect the course of the story and relationships with other characters. The game also has several mini-games and QTEs that add to the dynamics and suspense. The graphics of the game are not very realistic, but it has its own style and atmosphere. The soundtrack and character voicing are on a high level.

The game touches the player's emotions a lot, especially at the end of each episode. I'm not ashamed to admit that I let a tear fall at the end of the game when Lee and Clementine had to break up. It was one of the most touching and memorable moments in video game history. I am very grateful to the developers for this masterpiece and I recommend everyone who loves a good story and cares about the characters to play this game. It is well worth it.

words can't express how wonderful this whole game series including its characters is. the first season of The Walking Dead made by Telltale Games that was a beginning to this series is absolutely legendary and well deserved to be the game of the year back in 2012. this game is truly the best proof of being a legendary game that doesn't have epic graphics or gameplay. only the story, characters and their stories and all the details in this game series makes it amazing. if you're someone who enjoys wonderful and heartbreaking stories and want to experience that kind of thing in a game like me, this game series is made for you. Telltale just knows exactly how to make a "choices matter" story game. I've just had my 5th playthrough of the first season and the feelings and emotions are sill the same.

13 Years later and this game was just so ahead of its time for both game play and story telling. Yes hasn't aged the best in terms of quality and consistency compared to today's standards. HOWEVER, honestly the story telling, the unique art style and the characters, OMG the characters! The game stands alone on that. Lee and Clem's relationship is amazing and the ending will always make me cry.

If you like rich story games, this is a MUST!

The Walking Dead is a story-rich point and click adventure game both developed and published by Telltale Games. Take the role of convicted criminal Lee Everett as he suddenly finds himself thrust into the beginning of the zombie apocalypse. What would you do, how do you live and where do you go...these are some of the many questions that Lee must contend with? During his travels, Lee happens upon a young girl named Clementine and the two of them stick together as they must fight to survive this horror never knowing if death is just around the corner. This surprising 2012 Game Of The Year Independent title takes you on an emotional story full of suspense, exploration and meaningful choices as you struggle to stay alive in the unthinkable situation that you've suddenly found yourself in.

Whether you're fans of the television series or the comics then you'll definitely appreciate the episodic approach that Telltale Games took to the gameplay of this fantastic title. Each episode is like picking up a new comic or watching a new weekly television show as it's superbly presented with an excellent recap of events previous. The game itself is split into a five part series that takes Lee, Clementine and other survivors on a journey to different places and various situations as they desperately try to find some respite from the burgeoning zombie apocalypse during their quest for safe and permanent shelter. As the story progresses, you will be confronted with various choices to make sometimes in mere seconds that could truly mean the difference between life and death not only for you but for others as well so choose wisely. This is indeed where Telltale Games excels with their exquisite gameplay and riveting storytelling. In summary, this terrific approach to decision making alongside the emotionally driven narrative combine to create a gaming experience that is truly something special.

Visually, this title is nice looking and if I remember correctly it was also the first game in Telltale's fantastic stable of titles to use their striking artstyle which continues to this day. The game utilizes beautiful colors and fantastic animation combined with a wonderful cinematic narrative progression that manages nicely to immerse you within the always intriguing story. For me this truly excellent sense of immersion is one of the things that Telltale Games excels at. They really make you connect with the characters in the story and something like that always deepens the gameplay experience in my opinion. The art in this game reminds me very much of a comic book which is not a bad thing and quite appropriate considering that the "Walking Dead" franchise first got it's start as a comic. The sound quality is also very well done and adds alot in itself to the overall experience. You also get to visit a wide range of locales over the course of the five episodes of the game so that alone keeps the visuals fresh and interesting. In the end, The Walking Dead manages to expertly create a fantastic visual presentation to compliment the high emotionally charged and compelling narrative in this superb title. 

If you like the comics and the television show then you'll love this game...if you don't watch the show or have never read the comics then you will still love this game! The Walking Dead was a very enjoyable and unique experience for me. With this game Telltale introduced their fascinating method of immersive storytelling and it was well received and deservedly so. With choice and consequences being crucial in this title, the replayability is very high as different choices can and will lead to vastly different outcomes as well as death. The title also really made you care for the characters in the story which heightens the intenseness of the gameplay dramatically. As options go, there are Steam Achievements to be hunted down and Steam Trading Cards to collect as well as D.L.C. in the form of "The Walking Dead: 400 Days". This content tells a separate tale from the events of Season 1 yet with ripples of the decisions that you made in said season. In conclusion, boasting a riveting narrative, meaningful choices that usually must be made in only seconds and a visually appealing artstyle, The Walking Dead is HIGHLY RECOMMENDED to story-rich, zombie and post-apocalyptic gamers one and all!

The Walking Dead: Season One by Telltale Games is a masterpiece in storytelling that stands out as one of the best narrative-driven games. You play as Lee Everett, a man with a troubled past, who unexpectedly becomes the protector of a young girl named Clementine. The bond between Lee and Clementine is beautifully developed, making each decision feel weighty and personal.

The game captures the brutal reality of a world overtaken by zombies, where tough moral choices shape the story in significant ways. The story is intense and emotional, and it manages to balance hope, fear, and loss in a way few games achieve.

Although the gameplay is mostly point-and-click with some quick-time events, the real focus is on the characters and story. The graphics have a comic-book art style, paying homage to the original source material, and the soundtrack intensifies every key moment.

If you enjoy powerful storytelling and making meaningful choices, The Walking Dead: Season One is a must-play. It’s not just a game; it’s an emotional journey that will leave you thinking long after the credits roll.

The Walking Dead Season 1 is, in my opinion, the best storytelling experience that Telltale Games produced before their dissolution as a game studio. Out of the other seasons of the series, as well as their other storytelling games, The Walking Dead Season 1 has the most consistent and well-written plot, characters, and choices.

[h1]The Story[/h1]
The game takes place in the US state of Georgia. You play the role of Lee Everett, a history professor that is now convicted in the back of a police car after murdering a senator that slept with your wife. In the past few days, the zombie outbreak has started spreading. The police officer crashes the vehicle after hitting a zombie in the road and Lee is knocked unconscious. The infection has spread even further after Lee wakes up and comes face-to-face with the shambling corpses, now having to fend for himself in this new world and given a second chance after committing his crime. He comes across an 8-year-old girl named Clementine, who is all alone after her parents went on vacation to the city of Savannah and never returned. It's up to Lee to take care of her and help find her parents, as well as looking for a safe place to reside with fellow survivors amidst the apocalypse.

[h1]The Mechanics[/h1]
The game primarily consists of making choices for Lee, being "tailored to how you play". There are numerous actions and dialogue choices that the player can choose in order to shape Lee in their image. Whether you choose Lee to be a good-willed pacifist, a rude jerk, or keep choosing the "..." dialogue option, the choice is yours. Another common mechanic in the game is being able to roam around the vicinity and interact with people and objects in order to complete objectives to progress the story. The final mechanic in the game would be the QTEs (quick-time events), which are very common.

[h1]The Characters[/h1]
As Lee and Clementine look for a safe area to protect themselves from the zombie scourge, they come across many survivors, both friends and enemies; Lee can choose to side with or against some, or try to appease or alienate those that are already set in their ways about him. Many characters will start to form their opinion of Lee as they interact and through Lee's actions. Some choices will be bigger or smaller than others, but all of them matter in some capacity.

[h1]The Journey[/h1]
As the plot of the game progresses, Lee, Clementine, and other characters experience many emotions, being minuscule or life-changing. They experience joy, anger, loss, grief, shock, and most of all, death. Many characters come and go along the way, some being your friends and some being your enemies, but most of them will choose which they are based on your decisions. The story builds up to a climactic and tense conclusion, growing onto these characters and forming a bond with them through Lee. The ending to the final episode was the first time I had ever cried over a video game, specifically, over a character, and is a memory that sticks close to me to this day.

[h1]The DLC[/h1]
The Walking Dead Season 1 includes an extra episode that is unrelated to the main story. The story follows the paths of 5 survivors and their experiences as the zombie apocalypse reshapes the world, from the first few chaotic days of the outbreak to hundreds of days in when society has slowly rebuilt. These characters have a cameo in Season 2 based on your choices during their stories in order to try and make it feel more meaningful. Playing this bonus episode is completely optional and doesn't effect the story or your choices whatsoever, even in Season 2, save for the aforementioned cameos (though one particular character plays a more major role at some point).

[h1]Conclusion[/h1]
All in all, I feel that while Telltale's The Walking Dead is very lacking in the gameplay department, it makes up for it with stellar story and character development, actively engaging the player into interacting with the world around them, forming friendships and grudges against certain characters. Through the eyes of Lee Everett, the player experiences the zombie-infested world these characters reside and struggle to survive in, making both menial and thought-provoking choices as it continues based on what they believe is morally just. The game is tailored by how you play, and that tagline of Telltale's narrative-driven games very much holds up in this case.

In recent years we've seen a new dawn for the dead in video games and so it's perhaps unsurprising that The Walking Dead comic books by Robert Kirkman and hugely popular TV show by AMC has been given a video game release. Like a movie from the master George Romero, zombie games often have the word 'dead' in the title: If not walking, they are left 4, rising or on an island. However unlike a George Romero movie these games place very little emphasis on the previous lives of the zombies before they joined the ever swelling ranks of the undead. In all other zombie themed games I've played previously there is no sense that these infectious and deadly creatures were once your neighbours, your friends or even husbands, wives and children. Indeed by contrast the Walking Dead game is not an all out action game it is very much story driven and one requires as much watching as it does playing.

Your adventure starts with you (Lee Everett) convicted of murder being taken to jail. Whilst on your way to serve time for your crime the zombie apocalypse has started and a crash on the highway leaves you free but dazed, confused and surrounded by the hungry undead. I won't say much more about the plot but soon after you meet Clementine, a young girl left on her own and you will perhaps agree with me that she is one of the best characters ever created in a video game.

Throughout the episodes you will meet lots of other survivors and every charcter is incredibly well designed and accompanied by professional voice acting that is convincing and appropriate for the setting. The cel shaded art style fits perfectly with the comic book series really brings the characters to life. But the real beauty of the game is how you interact with other characters and how they ultimately relate to you, the decisions and the convesations that you have. There are a few crossroads that you find yourself at and you'll be forced to make a choice, quite often with very little time to consider the ramifications. Many choices have consequences and can mean life or death for those around you.

The game is played very much like a point and click adventure allowing you to examine objects and interact with other characters via a dialog option This play style is broken up with quick time style events when action is required which might be fighting off a zombie with a weapon or bare hands, escaping from an enemy, avoiding gunfire or accessing a building. It's a surprisingly satisfying experience and these action sequences can often be very tense and nerve-racking as you'll often find yourself in a mini panic as you struggle to survive.

This was an emotional rollercoaster and I found myself sat in silence pondering what I might of done differently as the credits rolled up the screen. Indeed, I was sad that experience was over and I was left wanting to find out more. What happened to a character in particular? I wanted and in fact needed to find out. I started season 2 and very much like a binge on Netflix found myself saying "just one more episode!"

My 2018 started kinda bad for me and I ended up sick hanging at my place for a week. During this time I understood one creepy thing - more games you have in your Steam library, then it becomes more difficult to choose what you want to play next, so I spent a lot of time trying to figure out which game I wish to play next. And I gotta be honest with you - it was hard and kinda stressful :)  

So, I decided to move forward with my Telltale Games marathon. And the next game was Walking Dead, obviously. Most of you will say, that it's a bit weird and you should start your introduction with this game, but there is a reasonable explanation. You know, I have never been a fan of zombie genre, neither a comic book nor a TV show fan and I tried to play Walking Dead a few times at least and always dropped it for different reasons.

The main reason, excluding my hate to zombie genre, was the unusual for these games difficulty and outdated feel, I mean playing this game after more fresh TT games can be a bit painful. There were few moments in this game when I really didn't know what do and what to grab to progress through the game, so I needed to check some guides and it was really awkward, like I never thought that I would be in a need to check walkthrough guides for any Telltale game.

Speaking of game itself, I would like to say, that it's a well made product, especially for someone who is in love with Walking Dead series. Game starts at the point, where you play as a Lee, murder convicted prisoner, who is riding on his way to prison in the police car. Straight at this moment the whole epidemic (or nonsense activity, whatever you call it) starts and you get into the car crash accident. You have a chance to escape now (well, obviously) and you do this (obviously, once again) . To show you, what this game will be about, you'll have to kill your first walker here,before you proceed and meet the second main character in the game. Like, everything to get you in the mood - some dialogues in the police car, some QTE with a zombie and then after you warm up, you are kinda ready to enjoy the game, pretty much simple, huh?

Another hero in this game is a small girl Clementine, who saves Lee's life and then you start your journey together. The more you play, the more their bound grows and they play that "we are team" card almost every episode for few times, which can be a little bit annoying. Major idea of this game and I believe, the whole Walking Dead universe, is to show us, how cruel people can be, when it comes to survival point and the biggest problem is not zombies/walkers at all, so you have to decide by yourself who to trust or not to trust during your journey and see what it will lead you to. 

Every character in this game has its own story and nature of its behavior, some of them can be really annoying, some of them will become your favorite and this can lead to fundamental outcome in your game. For me, Lee is still the funniest character in here - I can't stop laughing every time I see his emotional face with his eyes open wide, tryin' to show everyone how surprised/shocked/scared he is, but still this clown counts as a leader of the group, so I wouldn't say that I am a fan of the main character, definitely no. That guy never convinced me with his "tough-o-meter" high level.        

Be ready, that in this game choices really matter and sometimes you will be in a really uncomfortable situations. However, if anyone has to die, during the game scenario - he will die, no matter what and how hard you try, so no hard feelings. Also, I would like to state that this game has a DLC 400 days, which is really interesting and I enjoyed so much. It's super short, you can finish it in 40 minutes, I guess, but the way it tells you 5 linked short stories about this epidemic from different points of view is simply brilliant! 

Okay, to sum everything up.
You should grab this game if you:

+ Love Telltale games
+ Walking Dead fan (obviously), however this game have almost no connection to the show (I said almost, pay attention please)
+ Want to start your introduction to Telltale Games, this would be perfect game to start, don't make the same mistake as me, first 2-3 episodes are painful to play in this game after newest games 
+ Like story rich games with its twists and shocking scenes
+ Looking for a game where choices matter and you really feel like you want to play the game, where you tail your own story
+ Wanna have another +1 perfect game, just finish the game and you'll have it, easy as that, the only minor problem can be with 400 days DLC, but nothing too hard

Give it a pass if you:

- Don't like zombies 
- Are not ready to deal with outdated feel 
- Played some other Telltale Games and didn't like it, but still wanna try this because you are Walking Dead fan, trust me, it won't help

Enjoy!

The Walking Dead revolutionized episodic gaming by focusing on intense character drama and moral choices. The story centers on the deeply emotional bond between Lee and Clementine as they navigate a brutal apocalypse. Featuring a distinctive comic-book art style and outstanding voice acting, the game forces players to make gut-wrenching decisions that dynamically shape their relationships with other survivors.

There are really too few game elements in The Walking Dead to justify calling it a game. Its amazing world, great voice actors and the tough decisions it throws at you constantly will have you completely forget about this though. It's a compelling story that grabs you from the opening of the game and doesn't let go until its controversial ending in the last chapter. The intelligent choice-system  gives you the feeling that you're creating your own story, which is why you'll lose yourself in the characters in no-time. It never gets really challenging, but for those who enjoy a good story, it's a great enrichment of the Walking Dead-universe.

A memorable story in the Walking Dead world, rightfully highly praised! 

[h2]Lee & Clementine [/h2]
The story starts without knowledge of the dead. We are Lee, a convicted murderer, who is transferred to jail. He gets introduced that the world is drastically changing in a fitting manner. This apocalypse gives him a second chance at life, especially when he finds the abandoned child Clementine. 
While this happens in the same universe as the famous comic and the subtracted television series, this story is completely separate from that adventure. 

[h2]The first modern Telltale adventure! [/h2]
This game was such a success, that it created a format for many other games like this! Very recognisable style with cartboxy animations, and the illusion of choice. Many times you have to make some pretty hefty choices, for instance killing someone or not. But the result is almost never more than a change of one or two lines dialogue. They won't make several different stories, so if you chose not to kill someone, he or she will probably die in some other manner. 
Being the first game in this format, some parts are not fluent at all, and nearly come to a standstill. While other parts are very cinematic. 
As always with these Telltale games, the voice acting is outstanding! 

[h2]QTE...[/h2]
When I tried playing this seven years ago, I was pretty disillusioned... I have a progressive disease, meaning my muscles deteriorate until they don't work anymore. At that time I was stepping back from intensive games, discovering more chilled games. I started this game, then encountered the first QTE sequence, where you have to buttonbash and quickly react to actionprompts. I was furious! This isn't a cinematic point and click at all!! I get it, a feeling of urgency can enrich the experience, but is an option to turn it off too much to ask? 
This game (like other Telltale games) is great to experience second hand with a friend, even with someone who is not a gamer at all. So I tried it with my brother four years ago, but he couldn't push through a slower part of the game. I finally finished it with someone else this week. 

[h2]A classic!  [/h2]
The story is just great! You don't have to be into zombies to like this. While I don't think that this is the best Telltale game, this was the first of its kind. For me it feels like a classical section of gaming history, which any enthusiastic gamer should experience!

[h1]About the Game[/h1]

The Walking Dead game is a telltale game that tells the story of a man named Lee who is on his way to prison for committing a murder. The trip takes an unexpected turn as his life turn into a living hell.

[h1]Storyline/Gameplay[/h1]

Just like it's TV series counterpart. The Walking Dead game is not about killing zombies. There is barely an action in the game. TWD focuses more on the psychological effect of a world crisis into the human mind. The game will handle mostly about frustrations and being smart. You could say this game involves a lot of puzzle-like gameplay utilizing what's around to survive. The puzzles aren't that hard but it might be tricky for some and it can get really boring and repetitive. 

[h1]Mechanics[/h1]

[i]"This game is taillored by how you play."[/i]
True and false.
This is very misleading. Although changes are made when you pick different choices in the end it will go back to the linear storyline and proceed accordingly without taking your choices into account. From time to time, you'll see "<name> will remember that" but they do not have an impact to the game. The same thing basically happens just different dialogues.

[h1]Graphics[/h1]

The Walking Dead series gives off a thrilling atmosphere despite having intentional cartoonish textures and low-poly models. But overall, how the entire world and character are designed makes this game really good overall.

[h1]Final thoughts[/h1]

Although I gave mostly of the bad points in this game, I still recommend you to buy it especially with a discount. The story can really live an impression to some people and you might enjoy the horrific adventure.
